interfaces: Job build-and-test, check context 'CI / Build and test (Node)': actions/checkout@v4 with ref: github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha and fetch-depth: 0, npm ci, npm run build, npm test

Job schema-validation, check context 'CI / Schema and contract validation (Python)': actions/checkout@v4 with ref: github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha, python schemas/validate_fixtures.py, python schemas/validate_repository_contracts.py
Triggers: pull_request (branches: main), push (branches: main), workflow_dispatch

schemas/validate_repository_contracts.py: standalone script invoked as `python schemas/validate_repository_contracts.py`; exits 0 with 'PASS: <n> repository contract/task record(s) validated against their schema', or exits 1 with one 'FAIL: <path>: <reason>' line per violation

behavioralConstraints: both jobs (build-and-test, schema-validation) run unconditionally on every pull_request targeting main, every push to main, and manual workflow_dispatch; neither job is conditioned on which files changed

build-and-test's checkout uses fetch-depth: 0 (full history) rather than the action's default shallow single-ref clone, because tests/architecture-review.test.mjs and tests/qa-review.test.mjs run git merge-base against main/origin/main in the real checked-out repository (process.cwd(), not an isolated fixture repo), which is unresolvable under a shallow clone

both jobs' checkouts pin ref: github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha rather than the action's default pull_request-event ref (the synthetic merge commit GitHub computes, not the PR's actual head commit), so the exact commit tested is the same one a reviewer or a future merge-readiness reader means by 'this PR'
build-and-test fails if npm run build or npm test exits non-zero; a failing step halts the job rather than allowing a later step to report an independent success
schema-validation fails if schemas/validate_fixtures.py or schemas/validate_repository_contracts.py exits non-zero

schemas/validate_repository_contracts.py exits 1 when: a scanned contracts/**/module-contract.json or tasks/definitions/*.task.json file is not valid JSON; a scanned record does not validate against its corresponding schemas/v1/*.schema.json document; or zero contracts/**/module-contract.json files are found
schemas/validate_repository_contracts.py does not fail on zero tasks/definitions/*.task.json files, since the repository-native task registry may legitimately hold no records yet
no workflow step reads a checked-in 'evidence' or 'passed' file as a substitute for rerunning the underlying check; every reported result comes from that run's own process exit code

actions are pinned to major-version tags (actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4, actions/setup-python@v5); node-version is pinned to '20' matching package.json engines.node; python-version is pinned to '3.11' matching schemas/requirements.txt
a newer push to the same ref cancels an in-flight run for that ref (concurrency.cancel-in-progress: true) rather than letting a stale run's result be read after a newer commit exists for the same ref
invariants: this module performs no lifecycle-state transition, no merge, and no merge-readiness computation
this module decides no QA/Architecture/UAT judgment; it enforces only deterministic, reproducible checks
every check a job performs is also runnable locally with the exact command documented in docs/CI.md, so CI never depends on GitHub-only state
schemas/validate_repository_contracts.py never mutates a scanned file; it is read-only
examples: a PR that introduces a failing node --test assertion receives a failing build-and-test check; schema-validation is unaffected and still reports its own independent result

a PR that edits contracts/pr-lifecycle/module-contract.json to remove a required field (for example knownConsumers) receives a failing schema-validation check via schemas/validate_repository_contracts.py, identifying the exact file and the missing field
a clean PR that changes only documentation receives a passing build-and-test and a passing schema-validation, using the exact toolchain versions documented in docs/CI.md
a push directly to main reruns both jobs against that merge commit independently of whatever the source PR's last recorded run reported
edgeCases: a malformed (non-JSON) contracts/**/module-contract.json file fails schemas/validate_repository_contracts.py with a JSON-parse error identifying the file, rather than crashing the script or being silently skipped

if every contracts/**/module-contract.json file were ever deleted, schemas/validate_repository_contracts.py fails explicitly ('expected at least one file ... found none') rather than reporting a vacuous pass
a second commit pushed to the same PR while an earlier run is still in progress cancels that earlier run rather than letting a stale run's result be read after a newer one exists for the same ref

expectations: a success result for both jobs on a given commit means that commit's build, full test suite, schema fixtures, and real contract/task records all passed at that exact revision
acceptedRanges: each job's check status is exactly one of GitHub's own success/failure/cancelled/skipped states for that commit; this module introduces no additional custom status vocabulary
requiredReachableRanges: a success result must remain reachable for a commit whose code genuinely satisfies every check
a failure result must remain reachable for a commit whose code genuinely violates any required check
